title: Bridging the Temporal-Semantic Gap: A Trilingual Benchmark and Hybrid Retrieval Framework for Time-Critical Environmental, Social, and Governance Information Access​
abstract: Dense retrieval systems achieve strong cross-lingual semantic matching but fail systematically on queries with hard temporal constraints, a limitation we term temporal-semantic misalignment. This architectural failure persists even after fine-tuning on temporal training data, indicating the problem is structural rather than data-driven. To investigate this problem systematically, we introduce TemporalESG, a trilingual benchmark designed for evaluating temporal information retrieval in specialized domains. TemporalESG comprises 40,814 ESG disclosure documents across Vietnamese, English, and Arabic from 43 multinational corporations spanning 11 years (2015-2025), with 970 validated temporal queries. Evaluating six retrieval architectures against this benchmark, we find that state-of-the-art dense retrieval achieves only 65.1% temporal accuracy. Fine-tuning on over 7,000 temporal training examples yields only marginal recall gains while degrading top-ranked precision, confirming the limitation is architectural rather than data-driven. We propose a three-signal hybrid framework integrating BM25 lexical matching, dense semantic embeddings, and exponential temporal decay, which achieves 99.8% temporal accuracy and 50.8% entity precision across all three languages, with cross-validated generalization confirming these gains are robust. Our work establishes that hard temporal constraints require explicit architectural solutions beyond representation learning, a finding that extends to any domain where temporal precision is non-negotiable, including legal, medical, and regulatory retrieval.
